summary: Dynamic tier evaluation window causes micro-credit drift on hourly buckets
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a gradual, low-dollar discrepancy appearing in their hourly billing reconciliation for the last three billing windows. The discrepancy is ~0.1-0.3 credits per hour and aggregates to a visible line-item on their monthly invoice. The customer believes rate-tier evaluation during hourly rollover is classifying a small subset of toolcall requests into the wrong rate class (micro-rate drift).

Impact:
- Visible unexpected charge (~$12 USD/month at current usage) on LuminaAssist's billing export.
- Confusion for finance and internal SRE; customer concerned about correctness of automated-tiering logic for mixed workloads.

Environment:
- Production; us-east-1.
- Org: org-8462 (LuminaAssist).
- Dedicated plan with some hosted fallback traffic during peaks.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Run a scheduled batch of mixed chat+toolcall traffic that spans the top of the hour (e.g., 00:58–01:02).
2) Export hourly metering CSV from Console > Billing > Usage for the org.
3) Compare per-minute classification between minutes 58–02.
4) Observe ~0.1–0.3 credit difference in the hourly aggregate compared to total of per-minute records.

Logs / evidence attached by customer:
- Usage CSV snippet (lines included here show two toolcall events attributed to hour H but charged at the next-hour tier).
- Screenshot of invoice line for month with small line labeled "micro-tier adjustment".

Immediate ask:
Customer requests explanation of why there is a recurring small discrepancy and whether Redwood will adjust the invoice or provide a credit if a system classification bug is found.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Maya Chen: Acknowledged. Thank you for the reproduction steps and CSV. I have escalated to Billing Engineering and scheduled an initial triage. First response SLA logged.

2026-03-10 11:03 - Leo Alvarez (Billing Eng): Can you paste the CSV rows and the exact timestamp (ISO) for two sample events so we can trace them in postback logs? Looking for postback_id and rate_tag for the affected minutes.

2026-03-10 11:27 - LuminaAssist (Elena Park): Attached minimal CSV and the two event IDs: pb_23f4 and pb_23f5 (timestamps 2026-03-01T00:59:43Z and 2026-03-01T01:00:01Z). One appears in hour 00, one in hour 01 in our raw logs but both were billed at the higher hour-01 rate.

2026-03-11 08:45 - Leo Alvarez (Billing Eng): Found both postback entries. Postback processor applied candidate_rate="reserved-hourly-v2" on ingestion, but the tier-eval job applied final_rate="peak-toolcall" during the hourly rollover step. We are investigating the order-of-operations in the hourly materialization job.

2026-03-11 15:10 - Priya Nambiar (SRE): Reproduced locally with a synthetic stream that crosses hour boundary; observed nondeterministic tie-breaker in tier evaluator when event timestamp exactly equals hour boundary. Adding deterministic tie-breaker to evaluation logic as a mitigation step.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: The hourly materializer that collapses per-minute postbacks into the hour bucket runs a separate tier-evaluation pass during rollover. When events straddle the boundary (timestamp at or within 1s of the top-of-hour), the tie-breaker for rate-tier selection is non-deterministic due to race between ingestion timestamp normalization and the evaluation job's window assignment. Evidence: traced pb_23f4 (00:59:43Z) and pb_23f5 (01:00:01Z) — pb_23f5 was ingested with corrected timestamp but processed by a delayed worker that used wall-clock hour assignment. Workarounds identified: 1) disable on-the-fly reclassification during the hourly materialize and rely on ingestion-assigned tier, 2) apply deterministic floor(timestamp) assignment (always ceil-to-prev-hour) for boundary timestamps. Engineering ran a replay for sample hour and reproduced the 0.2-credit delta. Linked to race-condition change introduced in commit 1a2b3c4 (metering/tier-eval) rolled three weeks ago.
resolution_notes:
Mitigation deployed: Added deterministic tie-breaker (prefer ingestion-assigned tier when timestamp falls within 5s of hour boundary) and disabled reclassification pass for the hourly materializer in prod-us-east. Patch rolled to canary on 2026-03-12 and to full region 2026-03-12 02:15 UTC.

Customer outcome: We scheduled a targeted audit for LuminaAssist's affected hours for the last 30 days. Preliminary audit shows ~6.1 credits overcharge which we will apply as a one-time invoice credit. Finance is preparing a credit memo reference CM-2026-0421.

Follow-ups:
- Create a post-deploy job to backfill corrected hourly aggregates for affected orgs (task INT-8102).
- Add unit/integration tests that assert deterministic tiering at hour boundaries (ticket INT-8120).
- Communicate to Customer: summary, credit amount, and timeline.

Status: Customer notified of credit and engineering fix. Pending backfill and formal postmortem.
